findings.title: IAM policy uses NotAction with Allow effect
findings.description: Combining "NotAction" with "Effect": "Allow" creates a deny-bypass pattern: the policy allows everything EXCEPT the listed actions, which is the inverse of least privilege. Rewrite using explicit Action lists.

evidence.expected: explicit Action lists (no NotAction with Allow)

findings.remediation:
Replace `NotAction` + `Allow` with explicit `Action` lists. NotAction inverts
matching and is easy to misread — enumerate exactly what the identity may do
(see AEGIS-AWS-006 fix).

findings.title: IAM policy statement has no Sid
findings.description: At least one policy statement has no Sid, making the statement harder to reference in reviews, audit findings, and exception tracking. Give every statement a descriptive Sid.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.
